name: @yektoo/mcp-server

tools.name: list_email_accounts
tools.description: List all connected email accounts (IMAP and Outlook). Use this to get store_id values needed for filtering conversations. Each account has an id, name, email address, and type.

tools.name: list_shopify_accounts
tools.description: List connected Shopify stores and which email account each is linked to. The "id" is the shopify_store_id used by find_order, add_tracking and update_tracking. Shopify stores provide customer/order data — they are NOT email accounts.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List email conversations (threaded inbox). Returns conversations with an "id" field — use that id as email_id in read_thread, send_reply, close_ticket, etc. Each row includes customer_email, who sent the last message (customer/agent), and the assigned team member. Searches email bodies too. Results are paginated (20 per page by default). Tip: on large inboxes, filter by status/store/date for faster results.

store_id.description: Filter by email account ID (get IDs from list_email_accounts)

status.description: Filter by ticket status. Default: all

search.description: Search text — matches the email body (full-text, best for English), the subject, and the sender address. Use for order numbers, product names, phrases, or a customer email.

tag_ids.description: Filter by tag ID(s) (get IDs from list_tags). OR logic — matches any tag.

assigned_to.description: Filter by assignee: "me", "unassigned", a team member user_id, email, or name (see list_team_members). Default: all

folder.description: Mail folder. Default: inbox (spam is hidden unless requested)

page.description: Page number (default 1). Check has_next_page in response to know if more pages exist.

tools.name: list_open_tickets
tools.description: List only open/unresolved tickets for a specific email account. Requires a store_id — call list_email_accounts first to get IDs. Returns conversations with an "id" field usable in other tools, plus customer_email and assigned team member.

store_id.description: Email account ID (REQUIRED — get from list_email_accounts)

search.description: Search text — matches the email body (full-text, best for English), the subject, and the sender address. Use for order numbers, product names, phrases, or a customer email.

tag_ids.description: Filter by tag ID(s) (get IDs from list_tags)

assigned_to.description: Filter by assignee: "me", "unassigned", a team member user_id, email, or name (see list_team_members). Default: all

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: Read a full conversation thread — all customer emails, agent replies, and internal notes in chronological order. Every agent reply and note includes the team member who wrote it ("agent": {user_id, name}); "replied_by" summarizes who replied and how often; "tags" lists the conversation tags; "customer_email" is the customer's address for Shopify lookups. Use the "id" from list_conversations as the email_id.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations or list_open_tickets)

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: List everyone on the support team with their user_id, name and role. Use it to map names to user_ids for list_replies_by_agent or the assigned_to filter.

tools.name: list_replies_by_agent
tools.description: List replies sent from Yektoo across all threads, with the team member who sent each one, newest first. Returns a per-agent summary (reply and thread counts) plus the individual replies (email_id, subject, customer, date, preview). Use for questions like "who answered this customer", "what did Ana reply to today", or "how many replies did each agent send this week".

agent.description: Team member: user_id, email, or name (see list_team_members). Omit for all agents.

tools.name: send_reply
tools.description: Send a reply to the customer. It is emailed immediately (no review step) from the store's email account, formatted like the web app: paragraphs, the agent's signature, and {{variables}} filled from Shopify. If a {{variable}} cannot be filled, nothing is sent and the error says which. Use the "id" from list_conversations as email_id.

email_id.description: The conversation ID to reply to (the "id" field from list_conversations)

content.description: The complete message, sent immediately to the customer. Plain text with blank lines between paragraphs (converted to HTML), or HTML. Do not add a name/company signature — the agent's signature is appended automatically. {{template_variables}} are filled from Shopify.

signature.description: Append the agent's email signature for this mailbox (default true). Set false only if the content already includes it.

tools.name: reply_and_close
tools.description: Send a reply AND close/resolve the ticket in one step. Use when the issue is resolved and you want to send a final message. Same formatting, signature and {{variable}} handling as send_reply; if the reply cannot be sent, the ticket is left open.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations)

content.description: The complete message, sent immediately to the customer. Plain text with blank lines between paragraphs (converted to HTML), or HTML. Do not add a name/company signature — the agent's signature is appended automatically. {{template_variables}} are filled from Shopify.

signature.description: Append the agent's email signature for this mailbox (default true). Set false only if the content already includes it.

tools.name: close_ticket
tools.description: Close/resolve a ticket without sending a reply. Closes the entire conversation thread. Use reply_and_close instead if you also need to send a message.

email_id.description: The conversation ID to close (the "id" field from list_conversations)

tools.name: reopen_ticket
tools.description: Reopen a previously closed/resolved ticket. Changes the status back to open.

email_id.description: The conversation ID to reopen (the "id" field from list_conversations)

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add an internal note to a conversation. Internal notes are visible ONLY to support agents — the customer will NOT see this. Use for leaving context for other team members.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations)

tools.name: assign_ticket
tools.description: Assign a conversation (every email in the thread) to a team member, or unassign it. Same as the assignment dropdown in the web app.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations)

assignee.description: Team member name or user_id (see list_team_members), "me", or "unassigned"

tools.name: tag_ticket
tools.description: Add tags to a conversation (applies to the whole thread). Accepts tag names or IDs. Tag routing rules run as in the web app, so a tag may auto-assign the ticket.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations)

tools.name: untag_ticket
tools.description: Remove tags from a conversation (the whole thread). Accepts tag names or IDs.

email_id.description: The conversation ID (the "id" field from list_conversations)

tools.name: lookup_customer
tools.description: Look up a customer by email address in Shopify. Returns the customer profile (name, phone, total spend, order count) and their 10 most recent orders, each with ALL shipments and tracking numbers (fulfillments[].tracking[] with number, carrier and URL), the order status page URL, line items, payment status and shipping address. Use the "customer_email" field from read_thread / list_conversations. If nothing is found (customer wrote from another address), use find_order with the order number or tracking number instead.

customer_email.description: Customer email address (the "customer_email" field from read_thread or list_conversations)

store_id.description: Optional email account ID — limits the lookup to the Shopify store linked to that email account

tools.name: find_order
tools.description: Find Shopify orders by order number, tracking number, or customer email — across all connected Shopify stores. Returns each order with its shopify_store_id, id, all shipments (fulfillments with id + tracking numbers + carrier), order status page URL, items and shipping address. Provide exactly one of order_number, tracking_number, or email. Tracking-number search scans orders shipped in the last 180 days.

order_number.description: Order number as the customer wrote it, e.g. "#1234", "1234" or "YT1234"

email.description: Email address used on the order

shopify_store_id.description: Optional — limit to one Shopify store (from list_shopify_accounts)

tools.name: add_tracking
tools.description: Add a tracking number to a Shopify order by marking its remaining unfulfilled items as shipped (creates a fulfillment). Use when the order is unfulfilled or partially fulfilled. To change the tracking number on an order that is already shipped, use update_tracking instead. Requires the store's Shopify app to have fulfillment write scopes.

shopify_store_id.description: Shopify store ID (store.shopify_store_id from find_order / lookup_customer, or id from list_shopify_accounts)

company.description: Carrier name as Shopify knows it, e.g. "UPS", "USPS", "FedEx", "DHL Express", "Japan Post (EN)", "Yamato (JA)". Shopify builds the tracking link automatically for known carriers.

url.description: Tracking URL — only needed for carriers Shopify does not recognize

notify_customer.description: Send Shopify's shipping confirmation/update email to the customer (default true)

order_id.description: Order ID (the "id" field of an order from find_order / lookup_customer — NOT the "#1234" order number)

tools.name: update_tracking
tools.description: Change the tracking number / carrier on an existing shipment (fulfillment) of a Shopify order. Get fulfillment_id from the order's fulfillments list in find_order / lookup_customer. Requires the store's Shopify app to have fulfillment write scopes.

shopify_store_id.description: Shopify store ID (store.shopify_store_id from find_order / lookup_customer, or id from list_shopify_accounts)

company.description: Carrier name as Shopify knows it, e.g. "UPS", "USPS", "FedEx", "DHL Express", "Japan Post (EN)", "Yamato (JA)". Shopify builds the tracking link automatically for known carriers.

url.description: Tracking URL — only needed for carriers Shopify does not recognize

notify_customer.description: Send Shopify's shipping confirmation/update email to the customer (default true)

fulfillment_id.description: Fulfillment (shipment) ID — fulfillments[].id from find_order / lookup_customer

tools.name: check_shopify_access
tools.description: Diagnose what Yektoo can do in each connected Shopify store: the permission scopes its token actually has, whether order lookup, customer data (names/emails — Shopify "protected customer data"), tracking management and full order history work, plus how to fix anything missing. If the store's permissions were changed recently, this also fetches a fresh token so the new permissions take effect. Use it when find_order, lookup_customer, add_tracking or update_tracking report access problems.

shopify_store_id.description: Check one store (from list_shopify_accounts); omit to check all

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: List all email tags (AI Auto Tags and custom tags). Use the "id" field from results as tag_ids in list_conversations or list_open_tickets to filter by tag.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List all reply templates. Templates may contain {{variables}} like {{customer_first_name}} or {{order_number}} — send_reply fills them from the customer's Shopify data when sending (and refuses to send if one can't be filled). Use get_template to see full content before using in a reply.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Get the full content of a reply template. Returns both plain text and HTML versions, plus detected {{variables}}. Pass content_html (keeps formatting) or content_plain as the content for send_reply — variables are filled automatically when sending.

tools.name: get_csat_report
tools.description: Get CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) survey report — average rating, response rate, score distribution, per-agent breakdown, and recent individual responses.

instructions:
You are connected to Yektoo, a customer support helpdesk for e-commerce businesses.

IMPORTANT WORKFLOW:
1. To find conversations, ALWAYS start with list_conversations or list_open_tickets.
2. The "id" field in conversation results is the email_id you need for ALL other tools (read_thread, send_reply, close_ticket, etc.).
3. To get a store_id for filtering, call list_email_accounts first.
4. To get a tag_id for filtering, call list_tags first (tag_ticket / untag_ticket also accept tag names).
5. To get a template_id, call list_templates first.
6. Each conversation has a "customer_email" field — use THAT (not "from") for Shopify lookups. On outbound messages "from" is the store's own mailbox.

TEAM MEMBERS / WHO REPLIED:
- read_thread shows the author of every agent reply and internal note ("agent": {user_id, name}), plus "replied_by" (each team member who replied and how many times) and "assigned_to".
- list_conversations / list_open_tickets show "assigned_to" and accept an assigned_to filter ("me", "unassigned", a user_id, a team member's email, or their name).
- list_replies_by_agent answers "who replied to what" across many threads (e.g. "what did Ana answer this week?", "replies per agent today").
- list_team_members lists everyone on the team with their user_id.

ORDERS & TRACKING (Shopify):
- lookup_customer(customer_email) returns the customer's last 10 orders with EVERY shipment and tracking number (fulfillments[].tracking[]), carrier, order status page URL, line items and shipping address.
- find_order searches by order_number (e.g. "#1234" or "1234"), tracking_number, or email. Use it when the customer gives an order number, a tracking number, or writes from a different email than they ordered with.
- add_tracking(shopify_store_id, order_id, tracking_number, company) ships the order's remaining unfulfilled items with that tracking number.
- update_tracking(shopify_store_id, fulfillment_id, tracking_number, company) changes the tracking number on an existing shipment.
- shopify_store_id, order_id and fulfillment_id come from lookup_customer / find_order results. By default Shopify emails the customer the shipping update — set notify_customer=false to suppress it.
- Before adding or changing tracking, confirm the order and the tracking number with the user unless they have explicitly asked you to do it.
- If any Shopify tool reports an access/permission problem, run check_shopify_access — it shows exactly which permission is missing and how to fix it.

READING A CONVERSATION:
- Call read_thread with the email_id to see the full timeline of customer emails, agent replies, and internal notes.

REPLYING:
- send_reply / reply_and_close send the email to the customer immediately — there is no review step. Write the complete, final message.
- Write plain text with blank lines between paragraphs; it is converted to the same HTML the web app sends. HTML is also accepted.
- The logged-in agent's email signature for that mailbox is appended automatically. Do NOT add your own name/company signature block (a closing line like "Best regards," is fine). Pass signature=false only if the content already contains it.
- Template {{variables}} (e.g. {{customer_first_name}}, {{order_number}}, {{tracking_url}}) are filled from the customer's Shopify data when sending. If any can't be filled, nothing is sent and the error lists them — replace them with real text and retry.
- Replies are queued and delivered within seconds via the store's email account, attributed to the logged-in user.

ORGANIZING:
- assign_ticket assigns a conversation to a team member (name, user_id or "me"), or "unassigned".
- tag_ticket / untag_ticket add or remove tags (by name or id) on the whole conversation. read_thread shows current tags.
- Conversations in the spam folder are hidden by default — pass folder: "spam" (or "all") to list_conversations to see them.

IMPORTANT: Never fabricate email_id, store_id, tag_id, template_id, user_id, shopify_store_id, order_id, or fulfillment_id values. Always retrieve them from the appropriate list/search tool first.
